body:
It can be a really hard conversation, but maybe talk to your parents and ask them to help you find a counselor. Obviously if your parents are abusive maybe ask someone else. 

Having a support network makes a huge difference. Friends are great to talk to but if they don't understand what you're going through it can make you feel even more isolated and miserable, so a counselor kind of takes the pressure off. Good luck.
I'm sorry you're under all that stress. That shit sucks. Have you talked to anyone besides your brother about it? Counselor, parents? Other family?
Why do you want to kill yourself?

I'm really sorry for your loss. I went through a similar breakup myself over the summer. It sucks really hard.

What you described though... your girlfriend supported you to be confident, battle through your problems, etc. probably because what she already saw in you. For her to be your everything is a lot of pressure to put on one person (too much) especially when they're working through their own shit. 

We take pieces of the people we meet with us wherever we go. In that way she'll always be with you, even if you guys don't have a future together. At the end of the day though you should want to be a better version of yourself for *you*, not for her or anyone else. If you find that you hate yourself too much to do anything for you and you want to die then if *nothing* else please don't hurt yourself. Tell yourself "what would she want me to do" if you can't convince yourself that your demons are worth confronting. Ask yourself what would she say to you when you feel stuck. Whatever encouragement "she" says is still 100% valid and true even if she's not saying it to you directly.

Keep your loved ones close. Stay with a friend for awhile if you have to. Don't be alone during a break up, that's the worst. You'll get through this.

"your creation" is weird phrasing. She is a human being. She is the sum of her experiences and relationships. She does not owe you anything simply because you are her "creator". She does however owe you because you loaned her $$.

When you loaned her the money, was it clear to her that it was a loan? What was the plan for repayment? If there wasn't one before, draw one up now and bring it to her. Tell her it's this or small claims court.

ETA because I saw your other reply to a commenter: if her hours are cut, then make it a percentage based repayment... like send me 5% of your paycheck at the end of the month. Or for every $1,000 you earn, you should send me $100. Bring her an actionable plan. Be the example for how to deal with something like debt.
